# Promotion tracker

Maintains one tracker comment per application and full SHA in the source
repository. The helper passes the checked-out SHA, tracks automatic builds as
TVA, and tracks manual promotions using their destination environment.

Each environment row shows the latest attempt, UTC start and finish times,
the last successful deployment, actor, workflow attempt link, preview URL with
expiry, and live URL. A retry
does not erase the previous successful deployment or its URLs. An older attempt finishing
late does not replace a newer attempt's current status.

GitHub commit statuses under `vx-promotion/<app>/<environment>` retain the
events used to rebuild the table. Successful URLs are stored in additional
`vx-promotion-links/<app>/<environment>/<preview|live>` status contexts,
associated with their run and attempt. Pending, failed and cancelled attempts
never replace successful URLs. The comment marker identifies the tracker;
unrelated comments are left alone. Concurrent writes are reconciled with
fresh status reads. Duplicate trackers created by simultaneous starts are
consolidated when owned by the updating token. Another update can repair a
stale table because deployment events are retained separately.

The token needs **Contents: write** and **Commit statuses: write** in the
source repository. A workflow running there can use `github.token` with
`contents: write` and `statuses: write`. A workflow running in a different
repository uses a GitHub App installation token generated by the shared
[setup-source-auth action](../../common/setup-source-auth/README.md).

Centralized promotion needs the Actions variable `SOURCE_APP_CLIENT_ID` and
secret `SOURCE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` in `vx-fe-deployer`. Install the app on each
source repository with Contents and Commit statuses read/write permissions.
Validation and deployment jobs each generate their own temporary token.
TVA runs in the source repository retain their built-in `github.token`.
The selected source commit remains the location of the tracker.

The helper treats tracking errors as non-blocking. Cancellation is recorded
when the final tracking step runs; terminating a runner before that step can
leave an attempt marked in progress.

The Firebase action exposes the preview URL, preview expiry and live URL.
Static CDN sets `COMMENT_DEPLOYMENT: 'false'` and passes these outputs to the
tracker. Other callers retain the separate Firebase deployment comment by default.
